answer: On a terrace, agents book prism displays and echo tests. The venue offers no signup credits; agents buy single-use service vouchers instead. Each signed voucher binds a unique serial, service amount, expiry and owner key. Validators check issuer and owner signatures and expiry, then atomically mark its serial spent before supplying service. A copied voucher cannot fund a second request under another account. N identical requests need N paid vouchers, so aliases create no extra capacity. This removes signup farming, not wealthy attackers; legitimate users must pay too.
